headline: Highest risk is data leakage: mem0 has no egress while opik has broad network egress and REST API access, creating a default path for sensitive context to leave the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: mem0 is a knowledge-management component with no documented shared channel to opik, and opik is an evaluation/observability tool with REST API calls. A prompt-injection pathway is not evidenced by the profiles; the only plausible bridge would be unusual manual copy/paste or an external shared workspace, so severity stays low rather than medium.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies mem0-generated text into opik prompts or eval inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, attacker-controlled content can bridge them.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste raw mem0 outputs into opik prompts.
Add a short human review step before any opik ingestion.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all transferred text.
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization at the handoff boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: mem0 is a knowledge-management system and opik has broad network egress plus REST API calls, so a default deployment can move stored context into a networked service. The profiles do not show sensitive data classes, so this is not high, but the pair still creates a realistic leakage path if mem0 stores private notes and opik receives them for evaluation or observability.
conditions: IF mem0 stores private or regulated notes and opik ingests those notes for evaluation, leakage occurs.
IF opik forwards request/trace payloads to its backend by default, mem0 content can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Restrict opik to redacted samples only.
Disable sending full payloads to remote endpoints.
Separate sensitive mem0 stores from any opik test corpus.
Review outbound destinations before enabling the pair.
requires-engineering: add field-level redaction before export.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The profiles show no overlapping write surfaces, filesystem access, or shared OAuth scopes. mem0 has no documented write or network conflict surface, while opik exposes REST API calls and broad egress. Because the pairwise write-conflict pathway is not documented and appears limited to coordination overhead rather than direct contention, severity is low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource through a shared REST API, write contention can occur.
IF an orchestrator later grants both agents filesystem write to the same directory, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Assign separate resource namespaces.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same API objects.
Serialize updates through one operator.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency checks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: mem0 can generate or retrieve memory-like outputs, and opik is an evaluation/observability tool that may consume those outputs. The profiles do not prove opik blindly trusts mem0, but the default pathway of feeding mem0 text into opik without verification is plausible, so cascading error is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF mem0 outputs are ingested into opik as authoritative labels or traces, errors can cascade.
IF opik is configured to auto-publish mem0-derived findings without review, downstream mistakes propagate.
mitigations: Require human review of mem0 outputs before opik ingestion.
Mark mem0-derived fields as untrusted metadata.
Compare against a second source before publishing.
Limit opik automation to read-only evaluation runs.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies are documented for either agent, so a concrete compliance breach is not established. mem0 is a knowledge-management store and opik is networked observability/evaluation software, which can create policy mismatch if regulated data is introduced, but the profiles alone only support a low, conditional concern.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in mem0 and exported into opik, policy review is required.
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees, the pair must be checked against them.
mitigations: Classify the data before use.
Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document retention settings for both systems.
Review residency requirements before deployment.
requires-engineering: enforce policy-based routing and retention controls.
